script: I warned every guest, then the smoking rule exposed my darkest secret.. I was at the front desk, scrolling through the guest list when the fire alarm blared. That night shift alone, I swore I'd never vape in the hotel again. (I mean, who does that?). Later, my sibling—who also works here—texted me, "Need to fix a TV in room 305." I grabbed a spare remote and walked in. The room smelled like a secondhand cigarette lounge. "Smoking?" I asked. The guest said no, but when I pressed, he admitted it. (The audacity.) Our hotel's rules are posted everywhere: front door, side entrances, even at the front desk. I am the night auditor, so every check‑in I do includes a reminder of the no‑smoking/vaping policy and the extra charges. Yet nobody seems to enforce it. My boss is a pushover; he lets folks skip payments and even thinks we should charge people in the neighborhood to keep bad guests away. I tried showing him how we could add a prepaid hold for that, but he shrugged. Fast forward to 10:45 pm. Everything's calm until a guest checks in at 12:45 am. We're sold out, so we place him in room 302, right next to the one with the smoking issue. He storms down about 20 minutes later, whining about the smell. I tell him we're sold out and can't move him. He huffs, "Fine," and retreats. (You could say I am the best at keeping my cool.) After he left, I dug into the system. His room was 302. I slapped a $150 damages charge on his bill and wrote "Smoking in room" in the comments. He's set to check out tomorrow. I am already picturing his face when he sees the extra line. (I am literally the hero here.) That night, I came in at 11 pm and talked to my manager before he left. I told him I'd added the charge. He told me the hotel owner's son—another manager—had pulled it and even gave the guest a discount for the TV issue. (What the actual fuck?) I asked why we even have policies if we're not going to enforce them. He seemed irritated. On the registration cards, the no‑smoking rule is crystal clear. I am stunned that the charge disappeared. (Honestly, I am so done with this.)
